newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak 1997 wheat harvest to cover demand - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Slovak 1997 wheat harvest to cover demand - Minister.

text.p: This year's Slovak wheat harvest is estimated at over two million tonnes and will be sufficient to cover consumer demand, Agriculture Minister Peter Baco said on Thursday.

"We will have a wheat harvest of more than two million tonnes, we need some 550,000 tonnes for human consumption, so that a quarter of the expected harvest is needed for bread and we assume that we can reach this figure," Baco said in an interview with Slovak radio.
"The quality of the wheat is within the standard requirements," he added, but gave no further details or figures.

On July 28 the Slovak Statistical Bureau downgraded its estimate for this year's overall grain harvest to 3.03 million tonnes, from a previous estimate of 3.12 million tonnes, following heavy rains and floods.
Its total wheat harvest estimate at the time was over 1.9 million tonnes.
